checks: Compiled source mutant rejected by exact boundary test
Current typed relations and corresponding focused Rust tests are listed in adjacent model.md and model.md#evidence.
cost: Two linear passes: O(n) byte comparisons, O(n) output words, O(1) auxiliary words. Each successful comparison beyond the mirror lower bound advances the right frontier; at most one failed comparison per center. No throughput measurement.
forward: For byte sequence s of length n return odd/even vectors of length n. odd[i] is maximal r>=1 with palindrome s[i+1-r..i+r]; even[i] is maximal r>=0 with palindrome s[i-r..i+r]. The even center is immediately before i. Empty input yields two empty vectors.
inverse: Universe: finite byte inputs paired with arbitrary pairs of usize vectors. Excluded outputs have wrong lengths, zero odd radii, out-of-range spans, unequal symmetric byte pairs in a claimed span, or a radius whose next valid outer pair still matches. The model describes excluded behavior independently of negative tests.

Given two radius vectors of equal length n, compatible inputs are exactly byte strings of length n satisfying 1<=odd[i]<=min(i+1,n-i) and 0<=even[i]<=min(i,n-i), every symmetric equality inside every claimed span, and inequality of the next outer byte pair whenever that pair exists. Empty vectors admit empty input. Inconsistent equalities/inequalities admit no input; injective symbol relabelings exhibit nonunique antecedents.
limitations: Partial syntax; finite tests do not prove all inputs; byte rather than Unicode character semantics.
state: All finite byte slices and returned usize vector observations.
